## Documentary comparison

INFERENCE. `S-SCOPE-01` is consistent with the B profile. Slice 2 execution is **NOT DONE**. Slice 2 leaves open what happens after a reply is refused, whether a never-answered request remains asked, and whether literal admission uses the fixed slice-1 allowance.

SOURCE. The slice 1 decisions recorded in the bound disposition are:

- `ROW1-A O2(a)`. A refused reply does not resume the run. Record the attempt and retain the same pending request and continuation. The host may retry or end the run. Refusal adds no language failure.
- `ROW1-A O2(b)`. A never-answered request stays asked and waiting. With no terminal outcome, the dependent comparison is incomplete unless a separate irreversible mismatch is already established. See RUN1-003 A3 and A4.
- `ROW1-A O1(e)`. A literal check with the slice-1 bound uses one allowance common across hosts and runs, separate from execution fuel. The amount and charging protocol remain open.

SOURCE. The single B profile checks the complete program and selects the entry before creating the execution meter. Its preliminary reading, resolving and checking are unmetered. The checked forms and file-driven invocation expose no slice selector, language host request or reply entry point. The source-byte ceiling can report tool.source_limit. It is a tool limit. RUN1-004 T4 concerns the slice-2 first-call build. It and RG-003, RG-004, RG-006 and RG-007 supply no selected extension for these slice-1 policies.
